en: Theravāda Vinaya Bhikkhunīvibhaṅga Pācittiyakaṇḍa
Naggavagga 21.
The Training Rule on Being Naked.
At that time, the Buddha, the Blessed One, was dwelling at Sāvatthī in Jeta’s Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s monastery.
Now at that time, a number of bhikkhunīs were bathing naked together with courtesans at a certain ford in the river Aciravatī.
The courtesans ridiculed those bhikkhunīs, saying:
"What is the point, noble ladies, of practicing the holy life while you are still young? Should you not rather enjoy sensual pleasures?"
“When you have grown old, then you will practice the holy life.
In this way, both your purposes will be secured.
Being thus ridiculed by the courtesans, the bhikkhunīs were humiliated.
Then those bhikkhunīs went to the dwelling place and reported this matter to the bhikkhunīs.
The bhikkhunīs reported this matter to the bhikkhus.
The bhikkhus reported this matter to the Blessed One.
Then the Blessed One, having given a discourse on the Dhamma on this occasion and in this context, addressed the bhikkhus:
“In that case, bhikkhus, I will lay down a training rule for the bhikkhunīs, based on ten reasons—for the well-being of the Saṅgha... [and so forth]...”.
For the sake of supporting the discipline.
And thus, monks, let the bhikkhunīs recite this training rule:
“Whichever bhikkhunī should bathe naked, it is an offense entailing expiation (pācittiya).”
"But whichever" means whichever such... "nun" means...
[as before]... nun.
...pe... this is the nun intended in this context.
"She should bathe naked" means she bathes either without being clothed or without being covered; for the act of doing so, there is an offense of wrong-doing (dukkaṭa).
At the conclusion of the bath, there is an offense of expiation (pācittiya).
There is no offense for one whose robe has been stolen or whose robe has been lost.
In times of distress,
for one who is insane,
and for one who is a first-time offender.
The first training rule is concluded.
